html:
The Mohicans, or Mahicans, are an Algonquian people of the upper Hudson River valley in what is now New York, around present Albany, and east into western Massachusetts. Today they form the Stockbridge Munsee Community in Wisconsin.

In the early 1600s they traded furs with the Dutch at Fort Orange, the post that became Albany, and fought the Mohawk to their west for control of that trade. Losing these wars of the Beaver Wars era, many moved east after about 1680 to the Housatonic valley, where a mission town at Stockbridge, Massachusetts, was set up for them in 1734. They fought on the American side in the American Revolution, then lost their land and moved west to New York, Indiana and finally Wisconsin, joined by Munsee people. Their name reached readers worldwide through James Fenimore Cooper's novel The Last of the Mohicans (1826), though it mixed them up with the Mohegans of Connecticut. The map also shows them under the spelling Mahican.
